A. Acceptance Testing and Mobile Automation

   AT aims to validate a system’s behavior from the end-user        repositories, while the raw data layer connects to external
perspective. It complements other testing layers such as unit       sources like HTTP clients, GPS, and secure storage. The
and integration testing. Unit testing focuses on verifying in-      BLoC pattern separates business logic from the UI, promoting
dividual components, while integration testing ensures proper       maintainability and a clear separation of concerns [10], [11]:
interaction between different modules. Acceptance tests, al-        user events are dispatched to BLoCs, which process them,
though fewer in number, provide high-level assurance that the       interact with the domain layer, and emit new states for the UI.
application meets business and user requirements.
   Black-box testing forms the foundation of AT, evaluating
a system solely based on its external behavior without access
to internal implementation details [7]. Testers design scenarios
based on requirements and user stories, concentrating on inputs
and expected outputs. This approach is especially relevant in                  Fig. 1: MyBMW’s Three-Tiered Architecture
mobile applications, where user experience and business logic
must align closely with customer expectations [9].                    The test automation infrastructure for MyBMW uses Flutter

   Gherkin scenarios act as a crucial bridge between business     folds necessary imports, manages base class inheritance, and
requirements and technical implementation. Our system au-         integrates PageObjects to ensure consistency with BMW’s
tomates their generation by combining multiple sources of         testing framework. A final LLM validation step then refines the

for business context, code summaries for technical insight, and   from the business requirements (see Figure 3).
navigation paths to ensure realistic user flows.                     For each path, the system deterministically generates a
   The generation process is LLM-driven and adaptive. It          Kotlin test function. These functions leverage Page Object
can produce both simple scenarios and more complex edge           methods to traverse the application, access the target screen,
cases, depending on the depth and richness of the provided        and return to the initial state. This approach ensures that each
inputs. This flexibility is enabled through DeepSeek-R1, which    test executes in isolation while accurately reflecting realistic

structured prompts. AToMIC does not apply a hard limit               When corresponding Gherkin scenarios are available, a
during initial scenario generation. Instead, our approach gen-    code-specialized LLM (DeepSeek-Coder-V2) performs vali-
erates all plausible candidate scenarios and then, at posterior   dation and refinement of the generated test script. It ensures
phases in the workflow, applies multi-stage filtering: first,     alignment between test steps and the scenarios, removes

scenarios; second, LLM-based validation eliminates scenarios      clarity.
that are technically infeasible, redundant, or misaligned with       The final test scripts are placed into the appropriate module

                 IV. E MPIRICAL E VALUATION
   This section presents a comprehensive empirical evaluation
of the AToMIC system for automating acceptance test gen-
eration in industrial Flutter mobile application development.
The study was conducted using BMW’s MyBMW app, a
production system with over 170 screens.

A. Research Questions
  This evaluation aims to answer four research questions:
  RQ1: Accuracy and Completeness: To what extent are
         the generated artifacts accurate and complete when
         using LLMs for automating AT in mobile apps?
  RQ2: Time Efficiency: Is the process of generating ac-               Fig. 6: Traceability Tree Showcasing the Different Artifacts
         ceptance test scripts using LLMs more time-efficient
         compared to traditional manual methods?
  RQ3: Accessibility: How accessible and understandable
         are the generated acceptance test scripts for individ-           Page Object generation proved to be the most challenging
         uals with varying levels of technical expertise?              step. Of the 52 Page Objects generated, 78.8% could be used
  RQ4: Challenges and Limitations: What are the main                   without any manual modification. The remainder primarily
         challenges and limitations encountered when apply-            suffered from technical issues, incorrect inheritance from the
         ing LLMs to acceptance test generation for mobile             expected base class or imprecise function return types, which
         applications, and how do they impact the overall              in several cases required moderate developer intervention.
         process?                                                      While many fixes were straightforward (such as changing a
                                                                       single function signature), 7 Page Objects required deeper
B. Experimental Setup                                                  structural changes.
   The evaluation follows a mixed-methods strategy, combin-               Gherkin scenario generation achieved a 93.3% success rate
ing quantitative analysis with qualitative insights to provide a       (56 out of 60 scenarios valid), as determined by a syntactic val-
well-rounded view of AToMIC’s performance.                             idation of each generated file. This verification step was carried

pact on productivity, trust in the generated tests, and likelihood     within minutes. In practice, Gherkin scenarios were used as
of integration into regular workflows.                                 documentation and validation artifacts, reviewed by stake-

  The efficiency gains achieved by AToMIC were substantial.       LLM,” highlighting a potential limitation in highly specialized

Page Objects, and UI test scripts, took on average 259 seconds       Page Objects also received generally positive feedback,
per issue when executed locally, as shown in Table II.            though with some noted concerns. The main technical issues
                                                                  cited were related to inheritance hierarchy problems and
TABLE II: Average execution time and token usage per issue.       return type mismatches. Despite these challenges, respondents

 Artifact            Time (s)   Input Tokens     Output Tokens
 Page Objects         142.6        21,911            1,979
                                                                  practitioners reported that AToMIC could save “up to one full
 Gherkin Scenarios    100.5        11,263            4,334        day of work,” and one user remarked that “AToMIC will reduce

   To better understand LLM usage, Table II also shows the        respondents (100%) agreed that no manual adjustments were
number of input and output tokens processed by the language       needed after generation (as confirmed in qualitative feedback),
models. As expected, Page Object generation accounted for         and that the generated test cases were both accurate and well-
the largest share of execution time and token consumption,        aligned with the intended scenarios.
followed by Gherkin scenario generation.
   It should be noted that execution times can be reduced by
an estimated factor of 10x using cloud-based LLMs [19], to
approximately 26 seconds per issue, with an estimated cloud
cost below $0.01 per issue.
   From a practical standpoint, developer feedback strongly
supported the time savings observed. Several participants
estimated that tasks such as Page Object creation, which pre-
viously consumed hours, could now be completed in minutes.
Comments like “a full day saved” were not uncommon when
discussing repetitive test maintenance workflows.

E. Practitioner Survey and Qualitative Results
   To complement the technical evaluation, a practitioner sur-
vey was conducted using a convergent mixed-methods design.
This approach combined quantitative ratings and qualitative
feedback to assess the perceived quality, usability, and adop-
tion potential of AToMIC-generated artifacts in a real-world
industrial setting.
   The survey was distributed to nine practitioners directly
involved with the 13 JIRA issues. All participants reported            Fig. 7: Artifact Quality Assessment Survey Results
being at least “somewhat familiar” with the selected issues,
with 67% indicating they were “very familiar.” The respondent        2) Usability and Adoption: Practitioners reported that
pool was composed of seven developers, complemented by            AToMIC integrated smoothly into existing workflows. All
a Scrum Master and a Product Owner. In terms of expe-             participants agreed that the tool reduced the time required for

                                                                      RQ2: Is the process of generating acceptance test scripts
                                                                   using LLMs more time-efficient compared to traditional
                                                                   manual methods?
                                                                      Quantitative results show that AToMIC significantly reduces
                                                                   test generation time—averaging 259 seconds per issue lo-
                                                                   cally. Estimated cloud execution times suggest a potential
                                                                   10× speed-up, with negligible cost. In contrast, practitioners
                                                                   estimated a full day of manual effort per issue, yielding over
                                                                   95% time savings. These gains match or exceed results from
                                                                   comparable LLM-based studies [6], with no major bottlenecks
                                                                   and smooth workflow integration reported. It is important to
Fig. 8: Usability & Adoption Potential Assessment Survey           note that while automation inherently provides time-efficiency
Results                                                            benefits, these gains would not be as meaningful without the
                                                                   high quality of the generated artifacts.
